subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam now, and should its first non-Apple backend route through Gateway `tools.media.audio` or a separate native provider contract?
rationale: The issue is valid, but implementation would add user-visible backend selection, microphone-audio egress, credentials, fallback behavior, and overlay-state semantics that need maintainer product/security intent before code work is safe.

options.title: Design batch PTT seam first
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a batch-only backend boundary for PTT, and bridge to existing media-audio/provider contracts with explicit credential and fallback rules.

options.title: Fold into broader custom ASR design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a narrower slice while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 decides the shared native ASR provider contract across platforms.

options.title: Defer native backend selection
options.body: Leave native PTT on Apple Speech until maintainers decide custom ASR should stay outside the macOS app or behind plugin/Gateway surfaces only.

recommendation.title: Design batch PTT seam first
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a batch-only backend boundary for PTT, and bridge to existing media-audio/provider contracts with explicit credential and fallback rules.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history in the macOS PTT/Talk files and is already connected to the native voice path.
